Krugman's column cites Stanford economist Frank Wolak, an adviser to California's power grid, saying 'generators use forced outages strategically to withhold capacity from the market'. Krugman says a growing number of researchers share this view.
Per Krugman's column, FERC voted 2-to-1 on a Wednesday for new California price caps that apply only in emergency conditions. William Massey voted against, calling the caps ineffectual.

Krugman's column says the FERC caps have loopholes. Wolak calls one 'megawatt laundering': resale via affiliates or exempt imports. Severin Borenstein (UC Energy Institute) says pricing off the least efficient plant rewards inefficient generation.
Krugman's column says Wolak submitted a well-received proposal to mitigate the California crisis last fall, and that FERC ignored it.
